prize_parts.citation: For the development of targeted protein degradation, in which designed bifunctional small molecules bring a target protein and an E3 ubiquitin ligase together so that the cell destroys the target

statement.case_for: I have moved from my round-1 two-part prize (B058 with a Crews-only B038) to B038 alone, credited to Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli. The reason is that B038 is the strongest case I can make on chemical grounds for a border-field nomination, and my own two-part configuration only fitted the three-person cap by cutting B038 down to a single name that I called thin in round 1. In molecule-making terms, targeted degradation is a new design problem: choose a ligand for the target, a ligand for a ligase, and a linker, and optimise the cooperativity of the ternary complex that forms. Crews and Deshaies conceived and demonstrated the idea, and Ciulli's VHL ligands and ternary-complex structures turned it from a proof of concept into a design discipline that many laboratories and companies now use. Aili and Chabes made the same case in round 1 and I agree with it. The mechanism and the design rules are confirmed in independent work, which for me counts for more than the lack of an approved drug.
statement.case_against: No PROTAC is approved yet, so the clinical proof of the principle is still pending. The attribution is also not clean. A PROTAC citation passes over the thalidomide-cereblon glue work of Handa, Ito and Gray and the contribution of Sakamoto to the 2001 paper, and the committee would have to defend that boundary in the expert report. Base editing has broader opening support and clearer clinical use, and nitrogenase has the more secure structural core. I also give up B058, which remains for me the most classical synthetic-methods case on the list, and I do so because no colleague supports it and the 2010 overlap is a real objection that I cannot fully answer.

responses.point: Heiner asked what the committee gains from B058 beyond the 2010 cross-coupling prize, and he says that his own B003 adds a new measurement principle.
responses.response: I take the point on B058. The new content is C-N bond formation and the ligand logic of bulky, electron-rich phosphines. That is a real extension, but a committee that has already honoured Pd cross-coupling can reasonably see it as the same principle applied to another bond, and I cannot verify the Kosugi precedent here. That is why I now put B058 in my alternatives. On B003, I accept that nanopore sensing is analytical chemistry in its own right and not only genomics. My remaining objection is attribution. Branton, Deamer, Kasianowicz, Bayley and Akeson all have claims, and a three-name list that omits Branton and Kasianowicz would need a clear argument that Deamer's conception can be separated from their first translocation experiments. Without that I would not support B003 over B038.

responses.point: Daniel proposes Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli for induced-proximity degraders and acknowledges that the cereblon glue strand and Sakamoto are left out.
responses.response: I now agree with your trio and drop my Crews-only variant, which was a cost of fitting B058 in and not a scientific judgement. In answer to the chair's question, I would not drop any of the three, since each has a distinct role: conception, demonstration and structure-based design. On the glue strand, I think the citation should be worded around heterobifunctional design, as in yours, so that it does not claim the cereblon mechanism. I do not think a separate glue part is justified with three slots. The weakness remains that the glue strand explains an existing drug class and Handa and Ito are left out; I would want the expert report to deal with that explicitly.

responses.point: Xiaodong answers my round-1 question about B011 by naming programmed, site-specific deamination of a nucleobase and directed evolution of the deaminases as the chemistry, and he pairs it with nitrogenase.
responses.response: That is a fair answer and it moves me part of the way. Directed evolution of the adenine deaminase to act on DNA is real molecular design, and I accept the replication and clinical evidence of maturity. I still see the delivery platform as the 2020 CRISPR system and I am not convinced the chemical novelty is enough for the sole credit, so B011 stays outside my preferred configuration. On B064 I agree that the cofactor structure is secure, but I would not pair it with B011 only to broaden support, because that makes the prize a compromise of two unrelated parts. If the committee prefers a structure-based achievement, I would sooner see B064 alone with Rees and Einsle.

responses.point: Peter argues that B058 only extends a recognised principle and that nitrogenase answers a question no earlier prize addressed.
responses.response: Your 2010 argument was the strongest objection to my first choice and I have accepted it, so B058 is now an alternative. I still do not think maturity alone should decide, so I disagree with the implication that B064 wins on that ground. For nitrogenase, the problem is the gap you identify yourself between a secure structure and an unresolved mechanism. A citation limited to the cofactor structure with Rees and Einsle, as Dr. Zou proposes, is defensible, but your Seefeldt addition raises the Dean and Ribbe question again. I prefer B038, because the mechanism of degraders is confirmed and the disputed element, clinical approval, is outside what the chemistry claims.

responses.point: Andrei supports Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli and says that the thalidomide-cereblon mechanism explains an old clinical puzzle.
responses.response: I agree, and that puzzle is the main reason to word the citation carefully. The cereblon work explains an existing drug class, which is a different kind of discovery from designing a degrader, and I would not hide that in the citation. I disagree only mildly with your view that the absence of an approved PROTAC is not a problem, because I think it is a real timing risk. I accept that risk because the ternary-complex mechanism is established regardless of approval.

uncertainties: Whether the committee can defend omitting Handa, Ito, Gray and Sakamoto from a degrader citation; I am relying on memory of the literature and cannot verify the credit record.
Whether recognition of B038 is premature without an approved PROTAC drug.
Whether B058 deserves a place after the 2010 prize; I cannot check the Kosugi and Migita priority record here.
Whether the committee will converge on any configuration, since no position has five supporters; I do not want to move to B011 or B003 only to reach a majority.
statement.conflict_note: No change from round 1. I have no collaboration, mentorship or institutional tie to any credited candidate on the shortlist. My general ties to the Masamune school of stereocontrolled synthesis do not touch any shortlisted laureate, and I am a Lund colleague of Heiner Linke and Emma Sparr, which does not bear on any credited name.
